physical_mismatches.reason: No per-block floorplan geometry (x, y, width, height) or per-block power is published, only total chip area (109 mm2) and TDP (90 W). A Studio steady-state 2D thermal model cannot be built without splitting total power by an unpublished rule.

The paper's output metric is thermal-cycling lifetime (MTTF_TC), computed from transient temperature traces, rainflow cycle counting and long-term aging history. It is not a steady-state temperature field, so a steady-state Studio solve cannot reproduce it.

The controller is a dynamic closed loop with PID/MOC DVFS, PCPG, runtime application mapping and thread scheduling at ms to hour timescales. A static Studio solve has no equivalent controller or optimizer behavior.
The workload is time-varying and random (PARSEC applications entering and leaving at runtime). The power map is therefore transient and not a single fixed operating point.

The original thermal solver is HotSpot embedded in the Noculator/McPAT/Lumos simulation flow, and the package and cooling configuration is not described in the paper. The solver, boundary conditions and cooling therefore cannot be matched.
The scenario is a planar 2D many-core. No 3D stacking or interposer is involved, so there is no 3D or interposer mismatch.

studio_assumptions: No complete published floorplan and power scenario exists, so no Studio floorplan is produced (empty floorplan).
Any Studio bundled package, material, TIM, heat sink or boundary-condition defaults would be Studio assumptions and not paper-derived, because the paper specifies none of them.
The result would be a steady-state temperature estimate and cannot replicate the paper's MTTF_TC, controller or simulator behavior. No exact replication is claimed.
